genZNote: One of the only mosquito-borne viruses that can also spread through sex — and the reason pregnancy travel advisories exist for entire countries.

habitat.naturalHabitat: Maintained in a mosquito-primate sylvatic cycle in parts of Africa/Asia and a mosquito-human urban cycle elsewhere
habitat.hostAssociation: Transmitted primarily by Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus mosquitoes; unusually among arboviruses, also transmitted sexually and vertically (mother to fetus)

identificationClues: Diagnosed by RT-PCR in blood/urine during acute illness, or serology (with caution given cross-reactivity with other flaviviruses like dengue)
Most infections are mild or asymptomatic — low-grade fever, maculopapular rash, conjunctivitis, and arthralgia
Congenital Zika syndrome (microcephaly and other severe brain abnormalities) occurs when infection happens during pregnancy — the defining clinical concern
Unusual for an arbovirus in also being transmitted sexually and via blood transfusion, in addition to mosquito bites

diseases: Zika virus disease — usually mild febrile illness with rash, conjunctivitis, and arthralgia
Congenital Zika syndrome — microcephaly and other severe structural brain abnormalities when infection occurs during pregnancy
clinicalImportance.transmission: Aedes mosquito bite; also sexual transmission and vertical (mother-to-fetus) transmission, and rarely via blood transfusion
clinicalImportance.epidemiology: Caused a major international outbreak in the Americas in 2015-2016, prompting WHO to declare a Public Health Emergency of International Concern due to the surge in congenital microcephaly cases; travel and reproductive health advisories were issued for affected regions
clinicalImportance.labSignificance: Serologic cross-reactivity with dengue and other flaviviruses complicates interpretation, so RT-PCR is preferred during the acute viremic window, especially in pregnant patients with possible exposure

examFacts.distinguishingFeature: A flavivirus uniquely capable of sexual and vertical transmission in addition to mosquito spread, causing congenital microcephaly when infection occurs during pregnancy
